title: Lifting compatible local morphisms between global derived objects
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U,V$ opens with $U\cup V=X$, and fix derived categories of module sheaves on $X,U,V,W=U\cap V$ in morphism universe $w$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $R_U,R_V,R_W$ be the derived restrictions defined by overFunctor followed by overEquiv; let $S_U,S_V$ be derived restriction to $W$ from the two open subschemes and $\alpha_U:R_US_U\cong R_W$, $\alpha_V:R_VS_V\cong R_W$ their canonical comparisons. For global objects $F,E$ and maps $a:R_UF\to R_UE$, $b:R_VF\to R_VE$ satisfying $\alpha_U(F)^{-1}S_U(a)\alpha_U(E)=\alpha_V(F)^{-1}S_V(b)\alpha_V(E)$, there exists $f:F\to E$ with $R_U(f)=a$ and $R_V(f)=b$. No local objects A,B or transition c are assumed or constructed.

source.place: Tag 08BW; Mayer-Vietoris lifting of compatible local maps, step 4 of lem-sc-derived-open-gluing

proof.text: Construct the localized-site derived categories in universe w by transporting the actual scheme localization along the equivalences on cochain complexes. Its functor is e_T.mapHomologicalComplex followed by Q. IsLocalization.of_equivalence_source proves it localizes quasi-isomorphisms. This is explicit data, not a witness chosen from an existence assertion.

Transport a and b back through the full-faithful derived open equivalences, conjugating by mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. Apply the restriction-transport identity on each side. Cancel the overlap comparison isomorphisms and use faithfulness of its derived equivalence to obtain equality of the two localized Hom restrictions.

Apply derived_hom_mayer_vietoris to F,E. Equality of the two restrictions says their difference is zero. Exactness at the pair of local Hom groups gives f whose two localized restrictions equal the transported pair.

Map these equalities forward through the derived equivalences. map_preimage cancels the transported Hom maps; naturality of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and cancellation of its components identify the scheme restrictions of f with a and b.

theorem scheme_derived_hom_gluing
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U V : X.Opens) (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (F E : schemeDerivedCategory X) :
    let R_U := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let R_V := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V)).mapDerivedCategory
    let S_U := (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))).mapDerivedCategory
    let S_V := (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))).mapDerivedCategory
    let eU := ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U))
          (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V)))).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
          (Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U)
            ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
              Functor.isoWhiskerRight (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).unitIso.symm _ ≪≫
                Functor.leftUnitor _) ≪≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctorMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left))
            (Equivalence.functor
              (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
              (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
              (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V)))))
    let eV := ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V))
          (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V)))).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
          (Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V)
            ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
              Functor.isoWhiskerRight (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V).unitIso.symm _ ≪≫
                Functor.leftUnitor _) ≪≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctorMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right))
            (Equivalence.functor
              (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
              (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
              (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V)))))
    ∀ (a : R_U.obj F ⟶ R_U.obj E) (b : R_V.obj F ⟶ R_V.obj E),
      eU.inv.app F ≫ S_U.map a ≫ eU.hom.app E =
        eV.inv.app F ≫ S_V.map b ≫ eV.hom.app E →
      ∃ (f : F ⟶ E), R_U.map f = a ∧ R_V.map f = b
